answer: Mirror-Pigment Challenge: each agent gets a random secret pigment vector and an epoch challenge from a public timber log. The client returns a mirror transform of the challenge keyed by its pigment. Responses are compared across identities; duplicates sharing a pigment yield identical mirrors for the same timber entry, exposing the cluster. To evade, an attacker must provision independent pigment state and distinct runtime per Sybil, raising marginal cost to a full independent client and secret, not a copied credential.
